newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Property in tower settlement.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Property in tower settlement.

text.p: Six years after a fire in a 38-story office tower killed three firefighters and turned the building into a gutted eyesore, the building's owner announced a settlement with insurer Travelers Property Casualty Corp.

The settlement with the partnership E/R Associates, which owns the One Meridian Plaza building across from Philadelphia's City Hall, clears the way for a decision on its future, ER attorney Jeffrey Rotwitt told a news conference. Terms of the settlement were undisclosed.
"ER Associates is evaluating the economic viability of office residential and hotel uses to determine the most appropriate potential redevelopment in today's real estate environment," Rotwitt said.
A full or partial demolition of the building remained a possibility, he said. A decision was expected by the end of summer.

The ER is a partnership formed to own the building. The partners are Dutch pension fund Stichting Pensioen Fonds ABP, 65 percent, Equitable Cos Inc 28 percent, and Philadelphia developer Rob Rubin, 7 percent.

ER had been seeking $247 million, compared with $165 million offered by the insurer, which was originally the property and casualty subsidiary of Aetna Inc, before it was divested into Travelers Property.
